contents.p: About 10% of the population in the U.S has some type of learning disability.

tr.td: Processing information and interpreting complex charts and graphs.
Difficulties maintaining attention, are easily distracted, and find it hard to juggle multiple tasks.
Trouble with planning, starting tasks, and meeting deadlines, leading to difficulty with time management.
Problems with overall organization are common, affecting written work and efficient use of research services.

ul.li: Stigma: A stigma surrounds learning disabilities, causing people to feel ashamed or isolated and reluctant to seek support.
Mental Health: Work and academic struggles can lead to feelings of defeatism, stress, and other psycho-social issues, increasing the risk of dropping out and isolation.
Social Skills: Inconsistent perceptual abilities can sometimes affect the interpretation of non-verbal cues like tone of voice, impacting social interactions.
Lack of Awareness/Training: Many organizations receive insufficient training on accommodating students, workers and clients with learning disabilities, creating barriers to access.
Confusing Processes: People often find the process of applying for accommodations confusing and stressful.
Lack of Self-Advocacy: People, particularly those newly diagnosed, may lack the skills or awareness to effectively advocate for their needs.

contents.p: The image shows two side-by-side images of three children watching a baseball game from the outfield fence.

In the left image demonstrates equality since they all have a box to help them see over the fence. One child is tall enough to see over the fence standing on the box, the second child can only barely see over the fence standing on the box and the third child in a wheelchair cannot even get on the box.

The second image shows the same children in equity with the features they need to see the game. The tallest child with one box has what they need, the second child now has two boxes and they no longer have to struggle to see the game. The child in the wheelchair has a ramp so they can now see the game unobstructed.

ul.li: Inaccessible experiences and materials exclude people.

Accommodations are modifications or adjustments made for an individual with a disability on an as-needed basis, and give access to whoever is there at the moment, which requires extra work on the part of the person and the organization.
Accessible digital experiences and materials provide equal access for everyone without extra work.
